comment: Every place the document and the recording disagree, and every place this core is deliberately not claiming something. Each entry says what the document says, what the recording does, which one this package follows, and what evidence would settle it. Nothing here is averaged away or quietly resolved.

sources.document: Nintendo SNES Development Manual, Book 1, Appendix C. Pinned in hardware.json.
sources.recording: SingleStepTests/ProcessorTests, spc700/v1, pinned by commit in suites.json. 256 files, 1000 cases each, every cycle carrying an address, a value where the case names one, and a kind.

divergences.documentSays: Table C-11 gives MOVW dp, YA, code DA, as 2 bytes and 4 cycles. Read off the rendered page at 450 dots per inch to rule out a misread digit.
divergences.referenceDoes: All 1000 cases take 5 cycles, in the shape read opcode, read the operand byte, read the low destination byte and discard it, write the low half, write the high half.
divergences.reasoning: The discarded read is a store's read cycle, which every other store on this part also pays: MOV dp, A reads dp before writing it, and the recording shows the same shape there. A count with no breakdown cannot describe that cycle, so the document is not in a position to deny it. The document is also internally uneven here, giving the reading form MOVW YA, dp 5 cycles for two reads and the writing form 4 for two writes plus the same addressing work. A console now settles it. Shay Green's spc_mem_access_times.sfc checks which cycle of each of 172 opcodes touches memory against 8f 77 58 15, a value he took on hardware. Driven through the audio unit in sony-s-smp-python with its timers corrected, this processor produces 8f 77 58 15. The same run with MOVW dp, YA cut to four cycles, the discarded read removed, produces 2e a2 c2 0f. The check reaches this instruction and only five matches the console, so the manual's four is a misprint.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: Settled by a measurement taken on a console: spc_mem_access_times.sfc, SHA-256 53dc8005959d54ccfc95b8d4222e1d51d21e3d9f3491058320f105edc1a4454a, from https://gitlab.com/higan/snes-test-roms at commit 26e8aa91e0d3b90b901e7e693bc4a8244b391d7b, run on 2026-10-19. A second printing of Table C-11 would correct the document and would not change the answer.

divergences.documentSays: Table C-20 gives SLEEP, code EF, and STOP, code FF, as 3 cycles each. Page C-1 says of this part: "An SPC700 series is used for the SNES sound source CPU. However, standby and sleep modes cannot be used."
divergences.referenceDoes: Both record 7 cycles, in the shape read opcode, read the next byte, then idle and read that same byte again, twice more.
divergences.reasoning: Neither figure is a cycle count for the instruction, because the instruction does not finish. The part halts and repeats a read and an idle until something outside it intervenes, so a recording has to stop somewhere and 7 is where this one stops. The document's 3 counts the instruction up to the halt. This package reproduces the recorded shape so the comparison can run, and claims nothing about how long a halted part stays halted.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: Nothing would, and that is the point. The number is a property of where the recording was cut, not of the processor.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing. Appendix C gives a cycle count per instruction and no breakdown of what happens inside one.
divergences.referenceDoes: Names an address and a kind for every cycle of every case.
divergences.reasoning: Every placement in this core, which cycle drives which address, where the internal cycles fall, which reads are discarded, comes from the recording and from nothing else. The document can confirm a total and can never confirm a shape. Two cores agreeing with the document on all 256 totals can still disagree with each other on most cycles, which is why the total is the weaker claim of the two. Part of it is now held to hardware: spc_mem_access_times.sfc checks which cycle of each of 172 opcodes reads or writes memory against a value taken on a console, and this model reproduces that value. The other 84 opcodes, the addresses idle cycles drive, and anything a checksum of access timing cannot separate still rest on the recording alone.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A Sony datasheet for the SPC700, the S-SMP schematic, or a bus capture. Shay Green's reference table would name the 172 opcodes one by one rather than as a checksum.

divergences.documentSays: Nintendo documents the instruction set as a licensee-facing appendix. It is not a Sony datasheet and does not describe the silicon.
divergences.referenceDoes: Shay Green's spc_mem_access_times.sfc walks the instruction set on a console and checksums which cycle of each instruction touches memory.
divergences.reasoning: The disagreement was in neither this model nor the cut-down console the cartridge was driven from. snes_spc 0.9.0 and this family's composed model, handed the identical captured program with no console, both give 5e 71 f3 c3, which says only that they agree. With the whole cartridge driven through the audio unit, this model gave 08 42 1c 30 while the unit's timers restarted their prescaler on every enable and wrapped a lowered divider at once. Nintendo's Book I draws one prescaler feeding all three timers and says enabling a timer clears only its own two counters, with the divider matched by equality. With the unit's timers made to do that, the same cut-down console and this same processor give 8f 77 58 15, the console's value.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: Settled. The console's value is reproduced, and the run that cut MOVW dp, YA to four cycles shows the check is sensitive to this processor's cycle shape.

divergences.documentSays: Table C-16 gives BRK and RETI. Table C-19 gives EI and DI. No figure is given for accepting an interrupt.
divergences.referenceDoes: Never raises one. Every case runs one instruction from a state it declares.
divergences.reasoning: This core has no pin to raise an interrupt on, so there is nothing to model and nothing to check a model against. BRK, RETI, EI and DI are implemented because they are instructions; accepting an interrupt is not. The SNESdev wiki's APU pinout page, edited on 2026-10-04, lists all 64 pins of the S-SMP and the 24 of the sound module's connector and names no interrupt input on either. It is a community reading of a board rather than a document pinned by digest, so it narrows this and does not close it. Two S-SMP pins it names, T0 and T1, are not explained there.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A schematic of the audio unit pinned by digest, showing what T0, T1 and the two general ports connect to, a recording of the part with an interrupt line asserted, or a manufacturer figure for the acknowledge sequence.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing about what the registers hold at power on.
divergences.referenceDoes: Nothing. Every case declares a full initial state, so the suite never exercises a reset.
divergences.reasoning: A processor coming out of reset holds whatever it held, so this core scrambles the registers from a seed rather than clearing them, and reads the program counter from the reset vector. The scramble is deliberately not a claim about the hardware: it is a way to make a program that depends on an undefined register fail visibly instead of quietly working because everything happened to be zero. One flag is no longer invented. The direct-page bit is cleared on reset because the part's own boot program proves it must be: the sixty four bytes Sony put in the audio unit answer the console's handshake with `mov $f4,#$aa` and `mov $f5,#$bb`, which reach the ports only while the direct page is the zero page. With the bit set they would write ordinary memory at 0x01f4, the handshake would never appear, and no cartridge would ever get its audio program uploaded. That is the artifact answering a question the manual leaves open. Everything else in the flag word is still scrambled, because everything else is still genuinely undefined.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A capture of the register file coming out of reset on real hardware, for everything except the direct-page bit. That one is settled without a capture, by the part's own boot program: the handshake it answers with reaches the ports only while the direct page is the zero page, so a set bit would send it to ordinary memory and no cartridge would ever get its audio program uploaded. The rest of the flag word is still scrambled because it is still genuinely undefined.

divergences.documentSays: Chapter 22 and the sound chapters describe the timers, the four communication ports and the boot ROM that sit around this processor in the S-SMP.
divergences.referenceDoes: Treats the address space as flat memory. No case touches a port or a timer as anything other than a byte.
divergences.reasoning: This package is the processor. The registers at 00F0 to 00FF, the timers, and the IPL ROM belong to the S-SMP around it, and modelling them here would put two parts in one package and make the conformance comparison meaningless, because the suite reads and writes those addresses as ordinary memory.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: n/a. This is a scope boundary rather than an unknown.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing. Appendix C gives no value for the status word after a reset.
divergences.referenceDoes: Peter Lemon's seven SPC700 cartridges, SPC700ADC, AND, DEC, EOR, INC, ORA and SBC from https://gitlab.com/higan/snes-test-roms at commit 26e8aa91e0d3b90b901e7e693bc4a8244b391d7b, compare the whole status word after each instruction and expect the interrupt flag clear, though neither his program nor the boot program clears it. The mirror and his source make no claim that the expected values were taken on a console, so they carry no stated hardware provenance.
divergences.reasoning: This processor comes out of reset with the interrupt flag set from its scramble, which is not a claim about the hardware either, so a program that depends on the flag fails visibly here. A program whose expected values have no stated hardware source cannot settle the reset state, so the reset is left as it is. sony-s-smp-python's conformance/cartridges.py runs his cartridges with only that flag excused: where the status word his program compares differs from its expectation in the interrupt flag alone, the check is let through and recorded; any other difference fails.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A console reading the status word right after a reset, before anything sets or clears a flag, or a Sony document giving it.
